```{r}
# 1. Load the required packages
library(nlme)
library(survival)
library(JM)

# 2. Fit the longitudinal sub-model (using a long-format dataset)
# Track how a biomarker changes over time, grouping by patient ID
lme_fit <- lme(biomarker ~ observation_time * cohort, 
               random = ~ observation_time | patient_id, 
               data = longitudinal_data)

# 3. Fit the survival sub-model (using a baseline/one-row-per-patient dataset)
# Crucial: You MUST include 'x = TRUE' so the design matrix is saved
cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ cohort + age, 
                 data = baseline_data, 
                 x = TRUE)

# 4. Fit the Joint Model
# This links the shared random effects of both processes
joint_model <- jointModel(lme_fit, cox_fit, 
                          timeVar = "observation_time", 
                          method = "piecewise-PH-aGH")

# 5. View the integrated summary
summary(joint_model)


```
next to plot changes for separate chorts
```{r}

# Create individual patient profiles up to time 't' (e.g., 6 months)
patient_cohort1 <- longitudinal_data[longitudinal_data$patient_id == "Patient_A", ]
patient_cohort2 <- longitudinal_data[longitudinal_data$patient_id == "Patient_B", ]

# Predict future survival probabilities conditional on their biomarker history
curve_c1 <- survfitJM(joint_model, newdata = patient_cohort1)
curve_c2 <- survfitJM(joint_model, newdata = patient_cohort2)

# Plot the curves side by side or overlaid
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(curve_c1, main = "Cohort 1 Patient Survival", xlab = "Time")
plot(curve_c2, main = "Cohort 2 Patient Survival", xlab = "Time")
```

```{r}
# 1. Load the packages
library(nlme)
library(survival)
library(splines)
library(JMbayes2)

# 2. Fit the longitudinal eGFR sub-model (using a spline for non-linear time)
lme_egfr <- lme(eGFR ~ ns(observation_time, knots = c(1, 3)) * cohort + age + sex,
                random = ~ ns(observation_time, knots = c(1, 3)) | patient_id,
                data = longitudinal_data)

# 3. Fit the renal survival sub-model 
# Note: x = TRUE and model = TRUE are mandatory for JMbayes2
cox_renal <- coxph(Surv(time, event_status) ~ cohort + baseline_proteinuria,
                   data = baseline_data, 
                   x = TRUE, model = TRUE)

# 4. Fit the Joint Model
# By default, this links the true estimated eGFR value at time 't' to survival risk
jm_renal <- jm(cox_renal, lme_egfr, time_var = "observation_time")

# View hazard ratios for the event and fixed effects for eGFR
summary(jm_renal)

```
```{r}
# 1. Select a specific patient's longitudinal records up to year 2
patient_data <- longitudinal_data[longitudinal_data$patient_id == "Patient_101" & 
                                  longitudinal_data$observation_time <= 2, ]

# 2. Compute dynamic predictions (conditional on surviving past year 2)
pred_joint <- predict(jm_renal, newdata = patient_data, process = "both",
                      times = seq(2, 10, by = 0.1))

# 3. Generate the unified Joint Plot
# This automatically displays the eGFR trajectory on top and the survival curve below
plot(pred_joint)
```
